Issued at 1230 AM CST Thu Nov 5 2026

After yesterday's cold front passage, it wound up being a beautiful, 
fall day across South Texas, however, change is in the air. In the 
mid-/upper-levels, the subtropical jet is settling into place along 
the US/Mexico border and extending into the Southeast. At the 
surface, the cold front that moved through yesterday has now started 
lifting back north as a warm front, resulting in a weak, 
southeasterly flow allowing Gulf moisture/higher dewpoints to settle 
back into South Texas. This afternoon, this surface moisture 
advection, coupled with eastern Pacific moisture advecting in aloft, 
will increase PWATs to 1.6-1.9" values across South Texas and all 
preceding the next frontal passage overnight into Friday morning. 
While this will not bring a cooldown, what this will do is increase 
the moisture/surface convergence across the Coastal Bend. What will 
be the tricky part of the forecast tonight/Friday morning will be 
how far north the warm front lifts to as the further north it moves, 
the greater chance for instability to develop (CAPE increasing to 
500-1000 J/kg) and how strong will the bulk shear will be over South 
Texas. Latest hi-res guidance indicates that storm strength will be 
greatest as any storm that moves into the western Gulf waters, but 
any shower/storm that moves our communities has the potential to 
drop a quick 1-2 inches in rainfall. Most of this shower activity 
pushes south into Deep South Texas by the time the Friday morning 
commute gets underway. Friday is looking on the drier side with 
dewpoints in the 50s and 60s. Quite nice if you ask me.

While a nice Friday is in store, a positively-tilted trough will 
deepen as it moves through the Desert Southwest. Vorticity lobes 
will continue to pivot around this trough and into Texas, combined 
with the persistent subtropical jet streak across much of the state. 
All this to say, Saturday is looking to be on the soggy, initially 
across the Rio Grande Plains, and then spreading eastward through 
the rest of South Texas by Saturday night. These widespread rain 
chances (60-80% PoPs) will carry on into Sunday. As of this writing, 
NBM mean shows 48hr accumulations (ending Monday morning) shows a 
widespread 1-3 in rainfall amounts, with NBM90 coming in closer to 4-
6 inches. Note that the NBM gives the area between Corpus Christi 
Bay and Baffin Bay a 20% chance of exceeding 4 inches rainfall 
amounts Saturday/Sunday. For this reason, WPC has placed the region 
under a Marginal Risk for the Excessive Rainfall Outlook on Saturday 
and Sunday. While confidence is low for these higher-end amounts, we 
can't entirely discount them given the setup. As the upper-level 
trough approaches South Texas, a secondary surge of high pressure 
will increase northeast winds across the western Gulf waters to at 
times, near-gale conditions. We'll keep monitoring the latest 
forecast trends for wind magnitude to help decide which marine 
headline will be needed.

If all that wasn't enough and were hoping to go to the beach this 
weekend, it's not looking like it'll be a pleasurable experience. 
With the new moon approaching this weekend, combined with the 
northeast flow across our marine zones, will allow water levels to 
approach 2 ft above MSL as soon has the high tide cycle and 
continuing through the weekend. Latest P-ETSS guidance is showing 
that the water levels have the possibility of reaching 2.0-2.5 ft. 
Unfortunately, high tide cycles this weekend will occur in the 
afternoons/evenings, when people would be most prevalent on the 
beach. Please continue to check back and keep an eye out on local 
beach cams for the latest water level conditions.

After all that talk about precipitation associated with the cold 
frontal passages and the marine/coastal hazards, it's finally time 
to talk about the temperatures! Today's frontal passage will keep 
highs in the 70s/80s for Friday, but the big cool down will come 
Saturday and Sunday (though the front itself isn't the main reason 
while we'll remain in the 60s/70s this weekend (thank you rain). 
Rain chances decrease Monday into Tuesday as the trough moves into 
the ECONUS, allowing slight ridging influence to build across Texas, 
gradually warming temperatures back to near-normal values.
